title: Scale-dependent Fractal Analysis (ver. 0.1)
author: Ethan I Schaefer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmm2k48e

steps.title: Install Python Distribution
steps.instruction: Install a Python distribution that supports Python 2.7 and the required packages; Anaconda is suggested.

steps.title: Create Python 2.7 Environment
steps.instruction: Create a Python 2.7 environment using Anaconda.

substeps.instruction: Run the command 'conda create --name py2 python=2.7' in the Anaconda Prompt.

steps.title: Install Required Packages
steps.instruction: Install the necessary Python packages into the py2 environment.

substeps.instruction: Install numpy, scipy, matplotlib, and gdal using 'conda install numpy scipy matplotlib gdal'.
Optionally install the Spyder IDE using 'conda install spyder' to facilitate running the script and displaying plot outputs.

steps.title: Prepare Code Package
steps.instruction: Unzip the code package to a chosen directory path.

steps.title: Open Analysis Script
steps.instruction: Open the script 'FractalScript.py' in a Python editor (such as Spyder).

substeps.instruction: Locate the script at 'numgeo/scripts/fractal/FractalScript.py' within the unzipped code package.

steps.title: Configure User Settings
steps.instruction: Optionally edit the user settings located at the start of 'FractalScript.py' (ending at line 132).

substeps.instruction: Adjust settings for input data (e.g., shapefiles), fractal analysis parameters (e.g., number of iterations, size of the shortest rod), and plotting options (e.g., representative scale for the Richardson plot).
Note: If settings are not edited, the script will use example geometry data included in the code package.

steps.title: Run Fractal Analysis
steps.instruction: Execute 'FractalScript.py' to generate the analysis plots.

substeps.instruction: Review the three output plots: effective fractal dimension vs. geometric mean rod length, coefficient of determination vs. geometric mean rod length, and an example Richardson plot (measured length vs. rod length for a single geometric mean rod length).
Ignore any screen warnings or errors provided the plots are successfully outputted.
